problem: Existing 3D visual grounding methods rely mainly on geometric and visual cues (e.g. view selection), and existing 3D scene graphs carry only categorical labels and simple spatial relations. Both lack the multi-dimensional attributes (physical properties, affordances) needed for complex reasoning, and VLMs are queried from scratch on raw scenes.
motivation: Robots need a persistent, expressive yet compact world model that encodes object appearance, physical properties, affordances and relations for tasks such as fetching a specific fruit. Continuous first-person observations give multi-view evidence that can resolve geometric ambiguity and reveal latent semantics, so grounding can be turned into structured search over a pre-built map rather than free-form VLM querying.
key_idea: Build an online Diverse Semantic Map, a 3D scene graph whose nodes carry VLM-derived appearance/physical/affordance attributes and whose geometry is refined by a temporal sliding window, then ground queries by structured retrieval, relation filtering and multi-level rendered verification.
insight: Structuring the scene as a semantic-rich map lets the LLM/VLM reason over curated, pre-compiled context instead of raw noisy scenes. In the AI2-THOR ablation, removing Latent Relation Filtering drops overall Acc@0.25 from 61.59 to 54.77 (mostly on the Multiple category), and appearance is the strongest single attribute, though combining all three attributes gives the best result. The approach works across VLM backbones (GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-VL-7B/72B).
method: DSM definition: a 3D scene graph G=(O,R); each node has geometry (point cloud, oriented bbox) and semantics (identity, appearance/physical/affordance attributes); edges are spatial or semantic relations.

Single-view parsing: YoloWorld detection + SAM2 masks back-projected with depth/pose to object point clouds; GPT-4o-mini with visual prompting and CoT generates attributes and semantic relations; spatial relations come from point clouds.
Multi-view mapping: association score S = s_v (DINOv2 visual cosine) + s_g (3D IoU, fixed s_g0 if containment) + s_c (SigLIP text cosine), merged if above threshold T=1.5 (t_v 0.4, t_x 0.8, t_g 0.3).

Geometry Sliding Window: Monte Carlo-estimated viewing frustums over recent frames and a spatial voting scheme retain points consistent across views for denoising and shape completion; attributes and relations are updated by aggregation and voting.
Candidate Retrieval: an LLM parses the query into target, anchors and attributes, then candidates are matched against the DSM identities and attributes via text matching.
Latent Relation Filtering: an LLM scores the consistency between stored relations of candidate/anchor pairs and the query relations and keeps the top-k (k=3).
Multi-Level Verification: render object-, place- and scene-level views of each remaining candidate; a VLM makes the final choice given the images, attribute profiles and the query.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o-mini for map construction; grounding VLM is GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-VL-7B or Qwen2.5-VL-72B (all frozen); YoloWorld, SAM2, SigLIP, DINOv2
setting.observation: posed RGB-D frame sequences (time-continuous poses, depth and color)
setting.action_space: not applicable for grounding (outputs a 3D bounding box); real-robot demos use navigation to and grasping of grounded targets
setting.privileged: none stated (Nr3D/Sr3D evaluated with ground-truth boxes per the table caption)

numbers_note: No standard embodied-navigation benchmark is evaluated; the real-robot navigation and grasping demos are qualitative only. Dataset split names are not stated in the paper, so 'val' is used as a placeholder.
results: On ScanRefer, DSM-Grounding with Qwen2.5-VL-72B reaches 61.56 Acc@0.25 and 59.06 Acc@0.5 overall, beating the strongest zero-shot baseline FreeQ-Graph (56.13 / 49.41). It also achieves 62.19 on Nr3D and 73.33 on Sr3D and gets 67.93 F-mIoU on Replica segmentation, above the privileged OpenSeg (53.74).
limitations: Performance depends on upstream perception modules (detection, segmentation) and the quality of VLM-generated attributes.
High latency of large VLMs limits real-time use.
Evaluation is on a small ScanRefer subset (8 scenes), an unspecified backbone for Nr3D/Sr3D, and real-robot results are only qualitative.
